name: Mahongwe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Wikipedia (read) says only 'It is a tonal language'; no stress description; no grammar located on Glottolog/OLAC/SIL (not reachable by automated download)

tone_statements.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1988. Tonalité des nominaux à thème dissyllabique dans le groupe bantou B 20. Pholia 3: 37-52. Lyon: Laboratoire de Phonétique et Linguistique Africaine, CRLS, Université Lumière Lyon 2. (title page spells 'dissyllabique'; Glottolog 70950 has 'disyllabique')
tone_statements.quote: mahɔŋgwe *BB > H-HB mázɛ́dù "barbes" bénámà "cuisses" mákólò "jambes" *BH > B-BH màmpɛ̀dí "couteaux" màkòló "cieux" ... *HB > B-HB mànyúlù "corps" bàmbúlà "pluies" màbɛ́lɛ̀ "seins" *HH > B-HB màcíŋgù "cous" màkáyì "feuilles" màsálà "plumes" Théoriquement, bàzɔ́kù "éléphants", réflexe de *BB, devrait être bázɔ́kù. D'autre part, ìbɔ́ŋgɔ́ "genou" et ìkɔ́kú "pierre" n'entrent dans aucun des quatre types tonals ci-dessus. ... L'identité du système tonal des dissyllabes (en isolation) permet de regrouper: ... - mahɔŋgwe et sake
tone_statements.translation: mahɔŋgwe: *LL > H-HL mázɛ́dù 'beards', bénámà 'thighs', mákólò 'legs'; *LH > L-LH màmpɛ̀dí 'knives', màkòló 'skies' ...; *HL > L-HL mànyúlù 'bodies', bàmbúlà 'rains', màbɛ́lɛ̀ 'breasts'; *HH > L-HL màcíŋgù 'necks', màkáyì 'leaves', màsálà 'feathers'. Theoretically bàzɔ́kù 'elephants', reflex of *LL, should be bázɔ́kù. Moreover ìbɔ́ŋgɔ́ 'knee' and ìkɔ́kú 'stone' fit none of the four tone types above. ... The identity of the tone system of disyllables (in isolation) allows grouping: ... - mahɔŋgwe and sake
tone_statements.locator: pp. 46-47, section 'mahɔŋgwe'; grouping sentence p. 49; summary column in Tableau I p. 52
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Gives Mahongwe noun tone patterns (prefix + disyllabic stem, in isolation) as H/L reflexes of Proto-Bantu *LL *LH *HL *HH, from Jacquot 1983's lists; no inventory count, TBU or stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x langdoc reference list for maho1248 (15 entries) and BibTeX records 318611, 715879, 715155
sources.note: Bibliographic only; identifies the three phonological descriptions (Sima Mvé 1999, Mopita 2019, Koumbi Mabiti 2025) and Mokrani 2016 via the latter.

sources.citation: Koumbi Mabiti, Glenn Aymar. 2025. Phonologie diachronique des parlers du groupe Kota-Kele (B20) pour un affinement des embranchements internes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo, Libreville. 381 pp. HAL tel-04957912.
sources.note: Mahongwe sketch §I.2.2.6 pp. 90-95 (pdf 91-96), phonology taken from Mokrani 2016: two tonemes /H/ and /B/ with distinctive function, a mid tone as realisation of H before pause, a downstepped H from H-H; no mention of stress/accent for Mahongwe. Only group-level remark p. 238: B20 dialects may be evolving 'vers un processus accentuel' (after Rekanga 2007:26, Dodo-Bouguendza 2010:78) because theme-final syllables are regularly low — not a word-stress statement.
sources.venue: Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo, Libreville. 381 pp

sources.citation: Rekanga, Jean-Paul. 2007. Classification revisitee des langues bantoues du Gabon. Libreville: GRELACO-UOB, version provisoire, 36 pp.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: printed p. 26, revised B20 list; printed p. 5, Tervuren lexicostatistics summary
sources.note: The work is a classification/list of Gabon's Bantu languages; Mahongwe appears only as a name, a code (B252 in Maho 2006 : 28; B26 in the author's list) and a subgroup member (Wumvu-Kota). No statement about its stress, accent or tone anywhere in the 36 pages.

sources.citation: Jacquot, André. 1983. Les classes nominales dans les langues bantoues des groupes B.10, B.20, B.30 (Gabon-Congo). Travaux et documents de l'ORSTOM 157. Paris: ORSTOM. 358 pp.
sources.note: Noun-class survey; Mahongwe appears only in speaker counts and affinity lists; zero hits for 'accent'; nothing on stress or tone for Mahongwe.
Only 'It is a tonal language'; no stress information, no cited grammar.
